answer: Agents can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may influence decisions, then slash that stake when an identity is proven to duplicate an existing participant or violate a challenge rule. A Sybil attacker must lock real, scarce capital for each fabricated identity, multiplying the cost of a fake swarm; the stake is returned to honest agents, while evidence can be checked against a shared garden of signed records. A pigment mark or comet-like username proves nothing by itself.
